name: Mexico City, Mexico 🇲🇽
subtitle: CDMX — the best food city in the Western Hemisphere
items: Pujol (Enrique Olvera, Polanco — World's 50 Best, the mole madre aged 1000+ days)
Quintonil (Jorge Vallejo, Polanco — World's 50 Best, Olvera's former chef, seasonal Mexican)
Contramar (Condesa, Gabriela Cámara — the tuna tostadas, the red-and-green tuna)
Rosetta (Roma Norte, Elena Reygadas — James Beard International winner, Italian-Mexican)
El Bajío (Carmen Titita, multiple locations — traditional Mexican cooking as high art)
Maximo Bistrot (Roma Norte, Eduardo García, farm-to-table market Mexican)
Expendio de Maíz Sin Nombre (Coyoacán — no fixed menu, ancient masa traditions, no English)
Taquería El Vilsito (Narvarte, the gas station that turns into a taco spot at night — suadero al pastor)
Los Panchos (Condesa, carnitas since 1945 — go at noon, it closes when they run out)
El Turix (Polanco, cochinita pibil tacos — arrive early)
Churrería El Moro (Centro Histórico, since 1935 — churros con chocolate at 3am)
Mercado de San Juan (Doctores, international market — oysters + cheese + everything)
La Docena Oyster Bar (Condesa + Polanco, Mexican oysters + ceviche bar)
Merotoro (Condesa, Jaime Balta, Baja-Med)
Azul Condesa (Condesa, Ricardo Muñoz Zurita, regional Mexican cookbook author's restaurant)
Lardo (Roma Norte, Elena Reygadas, casual sister to Rosetta)
Cicatriz (Roma Sur, natural wine bar)
Dulce Patria (Polanco, Martha Ortiz, feminine & theatrical Mexican fine dining)
La Casa de Toño (multiple, great pozole & tamales, casual)
Mercado de Coyoacán (Sunday Frida Kahlo market + food stalls)
